claim.text: For the declared sphere-cap radial map F(theta,phi)=(lambda R theta,phi+omega), 0<Theta<pi, 1<= d_H(Fp,Fq)/(lambda d_S(p,q)) <= A(Theta)B(Theta) for distinct pairs, where A=sinh(a lambda R Theta)/(a lambda R sin Theta), and B=1 if Theta<=pi/2 else pi sin(pi-Theta)/(2(pi-Theta)).
claim.scope: One user-declared sphere-to-constant-curvature-hyperbolic radial map; spherical cap excludes south pole. Conservative cap-dependent upper factor, sharp lower factor.
assumptions: R>0, a>0, lambda>0 and 0<Theta<pi; finite positive declared length-unit conversion.
Source sphere and target hyperbolic plane carry their standard geodesic metrics.
A spherical geodesic ball of radius alpha=pi-Theta<pi/2 about the south pole is geodesically convex.
F is a smooth bijection from the cap to a hyperbolic disk.
forbidden_promotions: No claim of optimal global upper Lipschitz constant on nonconvex caps.
No assertion of canonical manifold transport, an isometry, or a sheaf connection.
No cap-size-independent finite upper bound as Theta approaches pi.
No inference that finite CI tests are a formal mathematical proof.

specification.intended_object: Typed global two-sided distance envelope with distinct lower, local-angular, boundary-detour and conservative upper factors.
invariants: detour_factor=1 on Theta<=pi/2; detour_factor=pi sin(pi-Theta)/(2(pi-Theta)) for pi/2<Theta<pi.
All factors dimensionless; source/target length-unit names remain explicit.
Passive rigid display-frame changes cannot change intrinsic bounds.
known_answer_cases: On convex caps new upper factor equals the earlier local-angular ceiling.
For opposite boundary points near south pole, ratio=(pi-epsilon)/epsilon.
For longitude gap pi on the excluded boundary circle, detour factor attains pi sin(alpha)/(2alpha).
